records.wording: NA27. Tertullian's "what he seems to have" (quod quis videatur habuisse) is cited by NA27 for Marcion (ὃ δοκεῖ ἔχειν, with Θ 69 syc.h**); Roth: possible only (cf. 8:18). Not adopted.

records.reason: "But as for these enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and slaughter them before me." Tertullian's point in 4.37.4 is that the parable shows God as a judge "even on the side of severity", and he finds that severity in the master taking away what the servant seemed to have (19:26). The command to slaughter the master's enemies would have been his strongest evidence, and he does not cite it. The verse ends the NA27 paragraph 19:11–27.
"After he had said this, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem." A one-verse NA27 paragraph with no attested verse; it introduces the entry (19:29–46), which Epiphanius says was absent.

witnesses.evidence: παρέκοψεν τὸ κεφάλαιον τὸ περὶ τῆς ὄνου καὶ Βηθφαγὴ καὶ τὸ περὶ τῆς πόλεως καὶ τοῦ ἱεροῦ, ὅτι γεγραμμένον ἦν »ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται, καὶ ποιεῖτε αὐτὸν σπήλαιον λῃστῶν«.

records.reason: Epiphanius states that the text lacked the section on the colt and Bethphage, the lament over the city, and the cleansing of the temple with its quotation "my house shall be called a house of prayer". Tertullian passes from 19:26 (4.37.4) to 20:1–8 (4.38.1); Roth counts his silence as confirmation (tacitus).
"He was teaching daily in the temple…" A separate NA27 paragraph with no attested verse (METHOD §4.3). Tertullian refers to his teaching by day in the temple only at 21:37 (4.39.19).
